Method/Site masking

Mobile element masking

Mask prophages, insertion sequences, and other mobile elements in a bacterial reference.

When to use this method

Use when

  • The organism is a bacterium whose genomes carry prophages, insertion sequences, or other horizontally acquired elements.
  • You want SNP distances and trees to reflect the chromosome's clonal history.

Combine with

  • Repeat and paralog masking: Add it when the reference also contains repeats such as rRNA operons or duplicated genes, which cause ambiguous read mapping.
  • Custom masking: Add your own BED file for species-specific regions that prediction tools do not find.

Operation

Site masking

Implementations

  • PHASTEST
  • ISEScan

Needs

Reference genome

Produces

Mask regions

Mobile elements move horizontally between lineages, so variation within them does not track the clonal history of the chromosome. Their coordinates are predicted on the reference and excluded from comparison.

Used by protocols

Specified by

  • Bacterial phylogenomic surveillanceStep 2 (optional)

Other methods for this operation

  • Custom maskingMask regions you define yourself in a BED file, such as genes known to be unreliable for your species.
  • Repeat and paralog maskingMask repetitive and duplicated regions of a reference so reads cannot map ambiguously.
